name: stdClassSum_rowStabilizer_eq
summary: Write both class sums as class integrals; the integral at the smaller level H is the index times the integral at K₀ of the sum over the cosets of H; with columnDatum_mul_ite_eq the coset sum of the datum Ψ_H is the datum Ψ, coset by coset.

steps.claim: Express the class sum at level H as (index)⁻¹ times a class integral (classIntegral_eq_of_le), that at level K₀ as a class integral (classIntegral_eq_classSum), and decompose the class integral over K₀ as the sum over the cosets q ∈ GL_b(O/𝔪)/H of the integrals of the translates by the lifts liftMod(q) (classIntegral_sum); the invariance hypotheses of these rewrites remain as goals.
steps.lean:
rw [stdClassSum, ← (eq_inv_smul_iff₀ (by simp)).1 (classIntegral_eq_of_le ?l ?s le),
    ← classIntegral_eq_classSum (Subtype.forall'.2 fun k h ↦ ?_), eq_comm,
    classIntegral_sum Finset.univ (fun _ ↦ .id ℂ) (fun q : _ ⧸ rowStabilizer φ w e ↦
    ↑(liftMod q.out)) (fun _ ↦ ⟨?l, isOpen_mono ?s isOpen⟩) fun h ↦ ?_]

steps.claim: Compute the index [K₀ : 𝔪.levelOfSubgroup H] as the index of H in GL_b(O/𝔪) (stdLevelIndex_levelOfSubgroup) and simplify the rational scalars.
Unfold and reorder the remaining goals.

Left invariance under rational points: for δ in U(I_b)(E), the kernel at δh equals the kernel at h, since the real component of δ fixes v_P (hP), the Weil action commutes with integration in the second variable (pairWeil_integrated_right, with the tame data of hα) and the theta functional is invariant (theta_rat_mul).
steps.lean:
· rintro _ ⟨δ, rfl⟩ h; refine .trans ?_ ((pairThetaKer ..).swap.theta_rat_mul _ ⟨δ, rfl⟩ h)
    nth_rw 1 [modKernelI, modKernel, modDatum, ← hP (ratEmbed _ δ).1, ← pairWeil_integrated_right
      (ha := hα.2.choose_spec.1), ← pairTheta_mul]; simp [modDatum, pairTheta, embFin, Prod.mul_def]

steps.claim: Introduce an element k of K₀ with reduction in the level (and the point h) for the remaining goals.
In each remaining goal (invariance under right translation by the level, and the identity of the coset sum with the K₀-summand):
steps.lean:
all_goals
    simp only [columnDatum_mul_ite_eq _ _ w e hF, ↓modKernel_mul_Kf_right, hα.apply_det,
      ← modKernelBilin_apply, ← LinearMap.sum_apply, ← map_sum]
    congr with x; rw [← x.fromCols_toCols]; generalize x.toCols₂ = y
    obtain _ | ⟨y, rfl⟩ := em' (IsUnit y) <;> simp_all [χ.map_nonunit, isUnit_iff_isUnit_det,
      ← mul_assoc (χ _), ← map_mul, ← det_mul] <;> norm_cast <;>
      simp_all [← QuotientGroup.eq, mul_mem_cancel_left]

steps.claim: rewrite the datum with columnDatum_mul_ite_eq (the product of the column datum with the indicator equals χ(det z)F(z⁻¹y) for z ∈ H and 0 otherwise), the transformation of the kernel under right translation by K₀ (modKernel_mul_Kf_right, hα.apply_det), and linearity in the datum (modKernelBilin, sums).
steps.lean:
simp only [columnDatum_mul_ite_eq _ _ w e hF, ↓modKernel_mul_Kf_right, hα.apply_det,
      ← modKernelBilin_apply, ← LinearMap.sum_apply, ← map_sum]

steps.claim: compare the data pointwise in x, written as (y′ | y) with y = x″.
steps.lean: congr with x; rw [← x.fromCols_toCols]; generalize x.toCols₂ = y

steps.claim: Split on whether y is invertible: if not, χ(det y) = 0 (det y is not a unit) and both data vanish; if y is a unit, both sides are χ(det y)·F(y⁻¹y′) summed over the same cosets, matched by the quotient relation (QuotientGroup.eq, mul_mem_cancel_left).
steps.lean:
obtain _ | ⟨y, rfl⟩ := em' (IsUnit y) <;> simp_all [χ.map_nonunit, isUnit_iff_isUnit_det,
      ← mul_assoc (χ _), ← map_mul, ← det_mul] <;> norm_cast <;>
      simp_all [← QuotientGroup.eq, mul_mem_cancel_left]
